extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers of Popular Science Monthly; readers interested in aesthetics, psychology/psychiatry, and applied biology/entomology
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluative standards and practical criteria embedded in Popular Science Monthly essays on (a) visual form and aesthetics, (b) clinical/psychological description of hysteria, and (c) biological control of insect pests using microorganisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactile_suggestions_in_visual_form
rubrics_metrics.description: The residue of tactile experience (alone or in combination with muscular sense) is traceable plainly in the charm of smooth and rounded surface; sculpture is characterized by 'bossiness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactual sensations contribute directly to the pleasure of form; smoothness and roundedness, and qualities suggestive of touch, are aesthetic assets in sculpture and visual form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human_skill_suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual perception includes suggestions of human skill: man views forms in relation to degree of skill needed to produce them; a perfectly straight line calls up a vague consciousness of artistic finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delicate forms and perfect regularity/symmetry satisfy a feeling for fine workmanship. Departures from regularity that suggest bad workmanship are distinctly unpleasant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human_and_organic_form_associations
rubrics_metrics.description: More circumscribed associations arise from vague resemblances to agreeable natural forms, especially the human figure; the eye values quasi-human attitudes in inanimate nature and plant-like characters in ornament (e.g., Corinthian capital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogies to human attitude and movement lend aesthetic interest even when art is not imitative; such associations are valuable but more concrete/limited than abstract associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ocular_movement_and_motor_experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Ocular movement (real or ideal) is a direct sensuous element in visual form; when significance is withdrawn (as in decorative arabesque) the pleasurable character of ocular movement becomes evident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eye movements and associated motor experiences enter appreciably into the delight provided by sculpture and architecture, though their importance should not be exaggerated relative to touch and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual_coordination_unity_proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual factor: coordination of numerous slightly pleasurable elements under agreeable relations of unity and proportion; direct sensuous elements (ocular/tactual) outweigh indirect associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty may arise from (a) the specially pleasurable character of elements (beauty of simple forms) or (b) having a large number of distinct aspects under unity (beauty of intricate forms). Psychology cannot yet assign precise relative values, so enumeration rather than measurement is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hysteria_not_primarily_eros
rubrics_metrics.description: Hysteria is a nervous disease and is not causally related to sexual passion or celibacy; romantic/erotic explanations are incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can study causes and symptoms of hysteria scientifically and without appealing to eroticizing narratives; avoid assuming hysteria is an erotic disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degrees_of_hysteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Hysteria manifests in every degree: light hysteria (almost imperceptible, a disposition/temperament) to grave hysteria (confounded with insanity, general paralysis, epilepsy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At institutions like the Salpetriere, severe cases are concentrated; light forms are common in daily life. Grave hysteria includes anaesthesia (total/partial), convulsive attacks, and delirium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional_lability_and_theatricality
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic symptoms include extreme and rapid swings of feeling (crying for nothing, sudden fits of sorrow or gayety), dramatic theatrical behavior, exaggeration of all emotions (terror, jealousy, joy, anger), and making everyday life into scenes fit for drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hysterical persons display highly changeable, impulsive affect, often with abrupt onset and disappearance; they lack transitions between emotional states and may appear 'picturesque' or theatrical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Somatic_symptoms_and_nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical manifestations include capricious appetite (often a marked taste for vinegar and green fruits), irregular/deficient alimentation leading to impaired nutrition and anemia which augments hysteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dietary habits can exacerbate hysteria via physiological pathways (e.g., anemia); practitioners should consider nutritional state as both cause and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will_impotence_and_deceptiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary psychical deficit is impotency of the will to restrain passion: hysterical persons are driven by passion, lack the power to regulate feelings, and are often deceptive or prone to inventing false details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intelligence, memory, and apprehension may remain intact; clinicians should note the contrast between preserved intellect and impaired volitional control; physicians must be alert to intentional or habitual deception in history-taking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hysteria_causes_heredity_social
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal causes include heredity (predisposition; nervous temperament transmitted across generations) and social causes (mismatch between education/aspirations and social reality leading to frustration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heredity does not require identical pathological forms across generations (e.g., epileptic father may have hysterical daughter). Social frustration, disappointed dreams, and urban conditions increase incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction_between_hysteria_and_insanity
rubrics_metrics.description: In insanity the intelligence is deeply affected, whereas hysteria is a form of disposition rather than disease of intellect; the will (power to restrain passions) is the most delicate and first affected in hysterical states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnosis should emphasize preserved cognitive faculties in hysteria vs pervasive cognitive impairment in insanity; focus on volitional control and symptom patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological_control_using_pathogens
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to destroy insect pests by encouraging spread of disease-producing fungi/bacteria fatal to insects (e.g., 'green muscardine'); such biological agents act as self-multiplying poisons that can be applied to infested plants/ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method aims to avoid acrid mineral poisons that damage plants; selecting pathogens that specifically infect target insects and can be mass-produced and dispersed is central to effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yeast_as_carrier_of_pathogens
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary brewer's yeast (beer-yeast) appears not to enter an insect's body to produce disease, but commercial yeast is often impure and may contain small quantities of other minute fungi (including spores of disease-producing parasites) which can act as infection sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical greenhouse practices using yeast may have worked not because Saccharomyces infects insects, but because contaminant pathogenic spores present in impure yeast were nourished by the yeast medium and thereby spread to insects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation_methods_for_muscardine_spores
rubrics_metrics.description: Green muscardine (Isaria destructor) can be cultivated apart from insects in beer-mash, producing rich mycelium and spores which might be applied to places attacked by injurious insects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass cultivation of pathogen spores in suitable liquid media (e.g., beer-mash) is a practical route to obtaining inoculum for field application; experimental proof of lethality to insects supports this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity_and_purity_considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all fungi/yeast strains infect insects; beer-yeast remains beer-yeast within experimental limits. Purity of supplies (as improved by Pasteur) affects whether yeast carries pathogenic contaminants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure strain selection and culture purity — contaminant pathogens may be present in impure yeast and supply infection, so deliberate use requires controlling identity and purity of cultures to avoid unintended effects.
